summary_zh: 之后又按正常面试题的写法重写了题干（中英文页都用英文题干），数字和条件不变。

issues.problem_zh: 原题干是一大段长句，把条件、规模、范围和要讨论的话题全挤在一起，读起来不像面试官会说的话；中文版又是逐句硬翻。
issues.change_zh: 按正常面试题的写法重写题干：先一句话说要设计什么，再分块列出已有条件、需求和规模、要交付什么、面试官会追问的话题和不考的范围。所有数字和条件不变，参考解答没有改。按用户要求，中文页的题干也直接用英文。

checked: read README.zh.md and README.md in full and compared them; the two say the same thing (every number in the prose matches across languages), their code blocks are identical, and the folder is byte-identical to the original
ran page (2 blocks, both languages pass)

recomputed every number independently (tools/out/scratch/b19/t8_google_calendar.py): 1.2e10 event rows, 2.4e9 recurring, 3,129 GiB (3.06 TiB) at 280 B; 694 / 3,472 write QPS and 5,208 / 26,042 view QPS, 7.5:1; 96 + 24x40 = 1,056 occurrences per 2 years, 1,188 in the 2.25-year window (90 days + 2 years = 2.246 years), 2,970 rows per user, 3e11 rows = 27 TiB at 100 B, 8.8x the event store; 3.6 rows per user per day -> 25 / 110 / 1,320 per week / month / year; 22 index rows per write, 76,389 row writes/s and 8,681 batches/s at peak; 60 series per viewer (also by counting participant-series pairs) -> 1.56M read-time expansions/s; 6.25 push targets per write, 3.75e8 pushes/day, 4,340 / 21,701 QPS; 4.5e9 change-log entries = 210 GiB

compared expand_series with my own expander (separate date generator, local-to-UTC conversion from a transition table instead of the fold attribute) on 6,000 random series in 14 time zones (30-minute DST, no-DST, far-east and far-west zones), with intervals 1-5, any by_day subset, by_month_day 1..31 and negative, by_set_pos including out-of-range values, start dates the rule does not generate, count, until on / just before / after an occurrence, cancelled and moved exceptions (moved into the range from later, moved out, moved before it), long events that start before the range: identical output in every case; the this-and-following split (old rule ends one second before, new rule gets count - k) reproduced the unsplit series in all 3,633 splits tried, including ones with cancelled occurrences before the split

ran each example in the prose: every 2 weeks on MO+FR counts Monday-started weeks from the start's week; a 31st-of-month rule skips April and June without using up count; last weekday = MO-FR with by_set_pos -1; a Tuesday 9 a.m. series keeps 9 a.m. while UTC moves an hour; 02:30 on the spring-forward day lands at 03:30 daylight time; 01:30 on the fall-back day is the first 01:30 and a one-hour meeting ends at the second; until is inclusive; a cancelled occurrence still counts; 105 / 730 / 24 rows for an endless weekly / daily / monthly series over two years

checked the RFC 5545 statements from knowledge of the RFC text: default WKST=MO, invalid dates ignored and not counted, BYSETPOS on the BYDAY set, UNTIL inclusive, COUNT and UNTIL mutually exclusive, DTSTART not matching the rule undefined, repeated local time = first occurrence, skipped local time = offset before the gap for a single DATE-TIME while recurrence instances at a nonexistent local time are to be ignored, EXDATE removed after the set is generated

simulated the all-day overlap-scan argument for every viewer offset from UTC-12 to UTC+14 in 15-minute steps: scanning from range_start minus the longest duration to range_end misses none of 55,755 overlapping all-day rows, and the key is at most 12 hours before the viewer's midnight, as the page says
checked the mermaid edges against the write and view walk-throughs (the out-of-window view's read of the event store is described in prose but not drawn - a simplification, nothing false)
